battle.name: 上下埃及的統一
battle.brief: 約公元前3100年，上埃及白冠之王那爾邁率南部諸邦聯軍北上，於尼羅河三角洲西緣擊破以紅冠為號的下埃及王權，完成兩地統一，並以孟斐斯白牆為新都。卡面這件早王朝埃及長矛正是本役裝備體系的骨幹：銅矛頭縛於木杆，步兵結密集隊形以矛近身，配石斧、弓矢與投擲棒；全役無戰車、無騎兵。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是上埃及與下埃及兩個政治體系之間的軍事統一，時間在約公元前3100年、即早王朝開端，戰鬥大致發生在尼羅河三角洲。上埃及一方以白冠（hedjet）為號，王權中心在南部尼羅河谷地的涅肯（希拉孔波利斯），其國王同時是守護隼荷魯斯的持有人，率領的是一個由王室直屬地、王室親屬村莊與一批地方首領組成的聯盟式王國；下埃及一方則以紅冠（deshret）為號，政治中心在三角洲西緣的布托，兩地各有一套自己的王名系統、王家祭祀與地方傳統。從軍隊與指揮系統看，兩邊都沒有獨立的將軍階級，統兵權就是王權本身：出征部隊以「持旗人」劃分，旗幟即部隊的識別與編制單位，王走在隊伍前部，親自擔任突擊的尖兵與破陣者；王室的直屬武裝與被納入聯盟的地方首領所部並肩作戰，後者的忠誠以歲貢、禮服與王室的宗教認可為交換，戰後則被收編為新王朝的封邑首領。宗教上，上埃及奉荷魯斯隼、下埃及奉瓦德杰特聖蛇為王權守護神，兩套神話同時被用來論證對方的王位合法性，這使得這場「統一」不只是攻城略地，還包括由誰來主持兩地的祭祀。
countriesEn: This war was the military unification of two political systems, Upper and Lower Egypt, fought at about 3100 BC, at the very beginning of the Early Dynastic Period, with the fighting taking place in the Nile Delta. The Upper Egyptian side wore the white crown (hedjet) and had its political centre in Nekhen, or Hierakonpolis, far up the southern valley; its king was also the holder of the falcon Horus, and he led a kingdom formed as a coalition of the royal estates, the settlements of the king's own kin and a body of local chiefs. The Lower Egyptian side wore the red crown (deshret) and had its centre at Buto on the western edge of the delta, with its own royal nomenclature, its own royal cult and its own local traditions. As for troops and command, neither side possessed an independent rank of general: the power to command the army was the royal power itself. The expeditionary force was divided by standard-bearers, the standard serving at once as the identifier of the unit, the reference point of the formation and the focus of its morale; the king marched at the head of the column, personally the leading point of the assault and the man who broke the enemy line. The royal troops fought shoulder to shoulder with contingents supplied by subordinate local chiefs, whose loyalty was exchanged for tribute, ceremonial attendance and the religious sanction of the crown, and who were afterwards absorbed into the new dynasty as the holders of fiefs. Religiously, Upper Egypt held the falcon of Horus and Lower Egypt the sacred cobra of Wadjet, each used to argue the legitimacy of the other side's kingship, which made this 'unification' something more than the storming of towns: it was also a question of who was to preside over the cults of both lands.
people: 主導這場戰爭並把自己的形象刻進石頭的人，是上埃及之王那爾邁，即後世史家所稱的美尼斯。他的名字寫在塞列赫（王名框）裡，用鯰魚與石鑿的寫音符號拼出「nar-mer」；而「美尼斯」這個名字是希臘化時代的轉寫形式，本身不見於當代遺物，學界普遍把兩者視為同一人。他在納爾邁調色板正面頭戴白冠，身穿無袖的短衣上衣，腰後繫著象徵王權的公牛尾，右手舉著石錘擊倒一名跪地的俘虜，腳下還有另一具屍身；反面則換上紅冠，排成行列出行。真正決定這場戰爭走向的，是他在戰後如何把一次軍事勝利轉成制度安排：在新都孟斐斯同時主持南方的荷魯斯祭祀與北方的瓦德杰特祭祀，把兩地王室的祖先神話並列於同一場「繞行」（環繞國土的儀式）之中，並以王名中「兩地綁合」的書寫反覆強調這一點。他並非第一個捲入北方衝突的人：早王朝之前的蝎子王已在調色板上留下開渠與向北用兵的痕跡，其後還有塞格等一連串名字延續同一條北進的傳統。那爾邁的戰果在身後被不斷重述，後世法老把這場統一當作王權合法性的起點，第十八王朝的塞努斯雷特一世等人曾以「統一者」的頭銜自我標榜。調色板上他身後那位捧鞋的近侍，被解讀為總督或王室高官，是畫面上唯一被具體描出的行政角色；反面隊列中的四名持旗人則是編制體系本身的寫照。
peopleEn: The man who led this war and carved his own image into stone was the Upper Egyptian king Narmer, the king whom the later historians call Menes. His name is written in a serekh, the royal name frame, as a catfish and a chisel forming the phonetic sign 'nar-mer'; the name 'Menes' itself is a Hellenised transcription and does not occur on contemporary monuments, and scholars generally treat the two as one and the same man. On the obverse of the Narmer Palette he wears the white crown, a sleeveless garment tied at the waist with the bull's tail that symbolises royal authority, and he raises a mace in his right hand to strike down a kneeling captive, with a second body lying at his feet; on the reverse he has changed into the red crown and marches in procession. What really decided the course of the war was the way he turned a military victory into a set of institutions after it: at the new capital of Memphis he presided over the cult of Horus of the south and the cult of Wadjet of the north together, setting the ancestral myths of both royal houses within a single 'Encirclement', the ritual circuit of the whole land, and he used the writing of the 'binding of the Two Lands' in his own name to underline the point again and again. He was not the first to be drawn into conflict in the north: the earlier king Scorpion had already left on his palette the trace of canal digging and of a campaign northward, and after him a string of names, such as Seg, carried the same northern tradition forward. Narmer's achievement was retold endlessly after his death, later pharaohs treating the unification as the beginning of legitimate kingship, and the king of the eighteenth dynasty, Senusret I, styling himself with the title of unifier. The attendant holding sandals behind the king on the palette, generally read as a high official of the court, is the only administrative character actually depicted; the four standard-bearers in the reverse procession are a picture of the command system itself.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛是本役真正用得上的兵器：早王朝的矛由一根硬木杆與一片銅或青銅矛頭組成，矛頭或為菱形、或為扁平葉形，以繃皮條或麻繩纏紮固定在杆端，沒有護手，重心偏低，適合密集隊形中的平推與近身刺擊；同一套形制在稍後的早王朝與古王國時期一直是埃及步兵的基本冷兵器。與之並列的還有：窄刃或扇形刃的銅斧與青銅斧，用來破開盾牌、斬斷頸部；銅匕首與燧石刀；單向反曲的弓，箭為木杆加燧石或骨製箭頭；投擲棒；以及石製的舍易特石錘，別在腰帶上當作日常護身之具。防護極簡：亞麻短衣，必要時加一領皮背心，早王朝尚無金屬頭盔，畫面中的裸露上身在埃及語裡的說法是「赤膊」而非無防備。攻城方面沒有任何可靠證據顯示當時埃及人使用過攻城塔或投石機，圍城靠逼近、封門、斷水斷糧與挖掘壕溝；盾牌的形制在早王朝並未定型。運輸與機動同樣有決定性：埃及的「公路」是尼羅河，部隊與糧秣靠船隊北上，順流而下讓上埃及軍隊佔盡便宜；馬匹在當時的埃及仍極稀少且不作戰用，既無騎兵也無戰車（戰車要等到第二中間期才由西索人引入），因此這是一場純粹的步兵與舟師之戰，長矛、斧、弓這三樣構成了全部的殺傷手段。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a weapon that genuinely saw service in this war: the Early Dynastic spear consisted of a shaft of hard wood and a copper or bronze head, either lozenge-shaped or a flat leaf, bound to the end of the shaft with thongs of hide or twisted cord, without any hand-guard, and low in balance, which suited the level push and the thrusting at close quarters of a close-packed formation; the same pattern remained the basic cold weapon of the Egyptian infantry through the later Early Dynastic Period and the Old Kingdom. Alongside it were the narrow-bladed or fan-bladed copper and bronze axes, used to break shields and cut at the neck; copper daggers and flint knives; single-recurve bows shooting arrows with wooden shafts and flint or bone heads; throwing sticks; and the stone sheyt pebbles, worn at the girdle as everyday protection. Protection was minimal: a linen tunic, at most a leather vest, and no metal helmet at all in this period, the bare upper body in the paintings being described in Egyptian as 'bare-backed' rather than as unprotected. As for siege work, there is no reliable evidence that Egyptian armies of this time ever used siege towers or stone-throwing engines; a siege was conducted by closing in, sealing the gate, cutting water and grain, and digging a ditch, and the shape of the shield was still not settled in the Early Dynastic Period. Transport and manoeuvre were decisive in the same way: the highway of Egypt was the Nile, and troops and provisions moved north in fleets, so that the current running downstream was an advantage entirely on the side of the Upper Egyptian army. Horses were still scarce in Egypt at this time and were not used in war: there was neither cavalry nor chariot, the chariot arriving only in the Second Intermediate Period with the Hyksos. This was therefore a war of pure infantry and river transport, and the spear, the axe and the bow made up the whole of its killing power.
tactics: 從納爾邁調色板與蠍子王調色板可以還原出這場戰爭的基本打法。第一是密度與旗幟編制：部隊以持旗人為核心，旗幟同時是編制標誌、方位基準與士氣憑依，隊形緊密，矛尖朝前，弓箭手在兩翼或前列提供覆蓋射擊，斧手與石錘手留在陣中處理殘敵與俘虜，王本人持錘走在最前。第二是水源與季節：尼羅河的泛濫決定了行動窗口，春季栽植期與秋季收穫期的水位最有利於舟師與陸軍協同，而蠍子王調色板上眾人揮鋤掘渠的場面，說明把運河挖成既能灌溉又能切割對方航路的工事，屬於當時的標準手段。第三是設防聚落：戰場調色板殘片上畫著帶垛口與塔樓的城牆，顯示下埃及的城邑是有防禦工事的；面對夯土牆，攻方能依靠的只有耐心、水源與士氣，而奪取城門的瞬間被記錄為「王舉錘擊倒跪地者」的定型姿勢，那姿勢不是寫實描寫，而是宣告勝負的儀式語法。第四是收編：真正把三角洲收進王國的，是把地方首領納入王朝體系、允許其保留祭祀與土地，同時以「兩地之王」「雙女神」「金荷魯斯」等頭銜把兩套守護神收編進同一王號，並以每年一次的繞行與塞德祭重申。第五是後勤：整個軍事行動都依賴河運，一支沒有戰車與輜重車的軍隊，其持續作戰能力完全取決於船隊能否緊貼部隊推進。
tacticsEn: The Narmer Palette and the Scorpion Macehead allow the basic method of this war to be reconstructed. First, density and the standard system: the units were built around standard-bearers, the standard being at once the badge of the unit, the datum of the formation and the focus of its morale; the ranks were close, the spear points forward, archers gave covering fire from the flanks or from the front, and axe-men and pebble-throwers stayed within the line to deal with survivors and prisoners, while the king himself marched at the head with mace in hand. Second, water and season: the Nile flood determined the window of operations, the water levels of the planting season in spring and of the harvest in autumn being those most favourable to the cooperation of fleet and army, and the scene on the Scorpion Macehead of men digging with hoes shows that cutting a canal which both irrigated and cut the enemy's line of navigation was a standard measure of the time. Third, fortified settlements: a fragment of the Battlefield Palette shows a wall with crenellations and towers, which shows that the towns of Lower Egypt did have defensive works; against a mud-brick wall the attacker had nothing but patience, water and morale to rely on, and the moment the gate was taken was fixed in the stereotyped pose of the king striking down a kneeling enemy with his mace, a pose that is not a realistic description but the ritual grammar of a victory announced. Fourth, absorption: what really brought the delta into the kingdom was the incorporation of the local chiefs into the dynastic system, allowing them to keep their cults and their lands, while the two guardian deities were folded into a single royal name through titles such as 'King of Upper and Lower Egypt', 'Two Ladies' and 'Golden Horus', and were reaffirmed by the annual circuit of the land and the sed festival. Fifth, logistics: the whole operation depended on river transport, and for an army with no chariots and no baggage wagons its capacity to keep fighting was decided entirely by whether the fleet could keep pace with the troops.
data: 可以寫實的數字大致如下。納爾邁調色板以灰色硬頁岩製成，高約六十三公分，現藏開羅埃及博物館（JE 27461），1897至1898年間由吉貝爾與格林在希拉孔波利斯廢城一座泥磚建築的牆基中挖出。正面有兩具屍身與一名跪地俘虜，反面刻著十具斬首的屍體、兩隻鷹隼與一排四名持旗人，末了還跟著一名捧鞋的近侍，這些是可以逐一核對的畫面元素；反面中央還有王名的塞列赫與牛形紋樣，說明「牛」是這一王室的象徵。地理上，尼羅河三角洲東西寬約二百四十公里、南北約一百六十公里，面積約二萬二千平方公里，分佈著沼澤、湖泊與不斷改道的汊流，軍隊能否在洪水期與收穫期之間的短窗口內通過，直接決定戰役的長度。年代上，佩特里的「序列年代」曾把統一置於約公元前3400年，現代分期則把它放在約公元前3100年至前2900年之間，卡面採3100年。曼涅托記載美尼斯在位六十二年（阿非利加努斯本）或三十九年（歐秀比烏斯本），巴里莫石碑把「洪水」與第三十年的塞德祭歸於這位開國之王。戰役本身的兵員、損失、持續時長與俘虜數目，在當時與後來的所有文獻中都沒有留下任何記錄，這一點只能照實說明。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The Narmer Palette is cut from greywacke, stands about sixty-three centimetres high, is kept in the Egyptian Museum in Cairo (JE 27461), and was excavated by Quibell and Green in 1897 and 1898 from the foot of the wall of a mud-brick building in the ruins of Hierakonpolis. The obverse carries two bodies and a kneeling captive; the reverse carries ten decapitated corpses, two birds of prey and a file of four standard-bearers, with an attendant holding sandals at the end of it, and these are elements that can be checked one by one. The centre of the reverse also holds the serekh of the royal name and a bovine emblem, which shows that the bull was the emblem of this royal house. Geographically, the Nile delta runs about two hundred and forty kilometres from east to west and about one hundred and sixty from north to south, covering some twenty-two thousand square kilometres, threaded with marshes, lakes and constantly shifting branches; whether an army could cross it in the short window between the flood and the harvest decided the length of the campaign. As to date, Petrie's sequence dating once put the unification at about 3400 BC, while modern periodisation places it between roughly 3100 and 2900 BC, and the card takes 3100. Manetho gives Menes a reign of sixty-two years in the epitome of Africanus or thirty-nine in that of Eusebius, and the Palermo Stone attributes the flood and a sed festival in the thirtieth year to this founding king. The strength of the army, the losses, the length of the fighting and the number of prisoners are not recorded anywhere, either at the time or later, and that can only be stated as it stands.
cause: 要理解這場統一為何會打成戰爭，得先看公元前四千紀末的尼羅河谷。當時南方的上埃及已經完成了對自己境內的整合，蝎子王調色板上的開渠場面說明南方王權的觸角早已伸入三角洲並且主動修築水道，換言之，衝突在所謂「統一」之前就已經爆發，只不過後來被重新講述為一場光榮的戰役。直接爭奪的東西有三樣：一是尼羅河的完整控制權，包括主河與三角洲各汊流，這決定灌溉的成敗，也決定誰能收稅；二是農業剩餘的分配，上埃及每年泛濫後產出的可存糧，是僱傭兵員、興修運河和供養軍隊的物質基礎，而這批剩餘的徵收權正是王位爭奪的真正標的；三是象徵性的王冠本身，白冠與紅冠各自有一套神話與守護神的支持，兩套王權的合法性在同一片土地上的並存本身就是矛盾。深一層看，統一也帶有經濟與技術的推力：把全流域的疏浚、蓄水與耕種納入同一套官僚調度，需要一個凌駕於地方首領之上的權力，而唯一有資格提供這個權力的，恰恰是一個已經統一全境的王朝。學界也提醒，不要把這場戰爭當成一次決定性的會戰：部分研究者認為聯盟式的整合在納爾邁之前已進行了數代人的時間，納爾邁做的更多是把既成事實寫成王朝的開端。
causeEn: To understand why this unification was fought as a war, one has to look at the Nile valley in the late fourth millennium BC. Upper Egypt by then had already consolidated the interior of the south, and the canal digging on the Scorpion Macehead shows that the southern crown had long since extended its reach into the delta and actively cut channels; in other words the conflict had broken out long before what was later called the 'unification', and was only afterwards retold as a glorious campaign. Three things were directly at stake: control of the whole of the Nile, main channel and delta branches alike, which decided whether irrigation succeeded and who collected the taxes; the distribution of the agricultural surplus, for the grain stored after each flood in the south was the material basis for hiring troops, cutting canals and feeding an army, and the right to levy that surplus was the real object of the contest for the throne; and the crown itself as a symbol, for the white crown and the red crown each had a mythology and a guardian deity behind them, and the coexistence of two legitimacies on one stretch of land was in itself the contradiction. At a deeper level the unification carried an economic and technical push of its own: bringing the dredging, storage and cultivation of the whole valley under a single administrative arrangement required a power above the local chiefs, and the only thing qualified to supply that power was a dynasty which had already unified the whole country. Scholars also warn against treating this war as one decisive battle: some hold that the coalition-like integration had been going on for generations before Narmer, and that what Narmer did was largely to write an accomplished fact as the beginning of a dynasty.
impact: 統一完成之後，埃及出現了幾乎所有後續三千年王權政治的基本框架。首先是「兩地合一」的國家觀念本身：把兩塊土地符號用繩索綁在一起的「兩地綁合」符號，既是那爾邁王名的含義，也是整個王朝時期王權的標準圖記，配合「兩地之王」「雙女神」等頭銜，把王對南方的統治與對北方的統治寫進同一個稱號裡。守護神也合流：荷魯斯隼與瓦德杰特聖蛇並列為「雙女神」，王本身則被冠以「金荷魯斯」之類的新頭銜。其次是中央集權的行政技術：孟斐斯的「白牆」成為固定的都城，王室直屬地與被收編的地方首領形成兩層結構，谷地與三角洲的稅收、徭役與水利調度被統一編排，這套機制後來在古王國時代成長為成熟的官僚與神廟經濟。第三是國家形式的紀錄：從王朝一開始，埃及才有連續可考的世系，王表、塞加拉王表與巴里莫石碑構成一條可以追溯的系譜，阿拜多斯與塞加拉的王陵墓地也成為國家祭祀的一部分。第四是後世的合法性話術：每逢需要為自身權位辯護，法老都會回到這場統一，把「兩地之王」作為王朝最古老而不可剝奪的權利來源，拉美西斯二世與塞努斯雷特一世仍以此為號召。第五是對外的秩序：全流域納入同一權力之下，使與蘇美爾、敘利亞、黎凡特的商旅往來有了可以預期的保護與收稅機制，這正是早王朝之後埃及在近東經濟圈中地位上升的原因。
impactEn: After the unification Egypt possessed almost the whole framework of royal politics for the three thousand years that followed. First and foremost the idea of the country as a union of the Two Lands itself: the emblem of the two land signs bound together with a cord is both the meaning of Narmer's name and the standard device of royal power throughout the dynastic period, and together with titles such as 'King of Upper and Lower Egypt' and 'Two Ladies' it wrote the king's rule of the south and his rule of the north into a single title. The guardian deities were merged as well: the falcon of Horus and the cobra of Wadjet stood side by side as the Two Ladies, and the king himself received new titles such as Golden Horus. Second, the administrative technique of centralised rule: the White Walls of Memphis became the fixed capital, the royal estates and the absorbed local chiefs formed a two-tier structure, and the levying of taxes, the assignment of labour and the management of the waters across valley and delta were arranged as one system, a mechanism that would mature in the Old Kingdom into a developed bureaucracy and temple economy. Third, the documentation of the state: from the First Dynasty onwards Egypt possessed a continuous line of succession, with the king lists, the Saqqara tablet and the Palermo Stone forming a traceable genealogy, and the royal cemeteries at Abydos and Saqqara became part of the national cult. Fourth, the rhetoric of legitimacy used later: whenever a king had to justify his own position he returned to this unification and treated the Two Lands as the oldest and most inalienable source of dynastic right, and Ramesses II and Senusret I still sounded that note. Fifth, order abroad: with the whole valley under a single power, traffic with Sumer, Syria and the Levant gained the predictable protection and the toll-taking that made it secure, which is precisely why Egypt rose in position within the Near Eastern economic circuit after the Early Dynastic Period.
result: 就軍事層面而言，這場戰爭的結果是上埃及的白冠王權在三角洲取得了決定性的優勢：下埃及的紅冠王國沒有被消滅，它的地方首領、祭祀傳統與王墓都保留下來，但獨立的紅冠王位從此消失，兩地之王的名號自王朝一開始就出現在王名中，紅冠也沒有被丟棄，而是與白冠合成雙冠，成為「兩地之王」儀式的一部分。制度上的結果是孟斐斯白牆的都城地位、王朝一世的連續世系，以及每年例行的繞行與塞德祭，這三件事把一次武力兼外交的結果固定成可以延續數百年的王朝秩序。過程上則必須說明：這並非一場在幾日之內決定一切的會戰。軍隊沿尼羅河北上要靠船隊，運河既是最後的補給線也是對方的阻斷手段，戰役的成敗在相當程度上取決於能否在泛濫與收穫之間的窗口裡把部隊送到三角洲；戰後還要花很長時間把地方首領收編進王朝體系。時間點上，傳統分期把統一定在約公元前3100年，卡面標記的月份取四月，對應的是洪水退去、三角洲可通行而收穫尚未入倉的季節，與開渠與北進在實務上互為因果的時序也相符。總結來說，這場戰爭是人類最早一批大型政治合併中的一件，其成果不是征服而是聯盟與祭祀的重組：南方王權吸收了北方的農業、航路與港口，也把自己的守護神擴展成全境的神，最終形成以「兩地」為單位、以王為唯一中心的埃及國家。卡面這件早王朝的埃及長矛因此不是一件象徵性的古董，而是這套步兵體系真正的骨架。
resultEn: At the military level, the result of this war was the decisive advantage of the white-crowned power of Upper Egypt in the delta: the red-crowned kingdom of Lower Egypt was not destroyed, its local chiefs, its cult traditions and its royal tombs all survived, but the independent red-crowned kingship was gone, the title of king of the Two Lands appears in the royal names from the very first dynasty, and the red crown was not discarded but combined with the white crown into the double crown, becoming part of the ritual of the Two Lands. The institutional result was the fixed capital at the White Walls of Memphis, the continuous line of the First Dynasty, and the annual circuit of the land and the sed festival; those three things turned a result won by arms and diplomacy alike into a dynastic order that could run for hundreds of years. As to the process, it must be said that this was not a battle decided in a few days. The army needed its fleet to move north along the Nile, canals were at once the last line of supply and the means of cutting the enemy off, and the outcome depended in large measure on whether the troops could be brought to the delta in the window between flood and harvest; and after the fighting a long time was needed to absorb the local chiefs into the dynastic system. As to timing, the traditional periodisation fixes the unification at about 3100 BC, and the month given on the card is the fourth, corresponding to the season in which the flood had receded, the delta was passable and the harvest was not yet in the granary, a sequence that also fits the practical interrelation between canal digging and the northward advance. In sum, this war is one of the earliest large political mergers in human history, and its outcome was not conquest but the restructuring of alliance and cult: the southern crown took in the agriculture, the waterways and the harbours of the north, extended its own guardian deity over the whole country, and so built an Egyptian state whose unit was the Two Lands and whose single centre was the king. The Early Dynastic Egyptian spear on the card is therefore not a symbolic antique, but the true backbone of that infantry system.
